title: Ted Tschopp's AI News
description: Latest AI News and Ratings from Ted Tschopp

items.title: Building Self-Improving Tax Agents with Codex [ ! ]
items.content_text: OpenAI and Thrive Holdings built Tax AI for Crete accountants, using Codex, practitioner feedback, production traces, and evals to improve tax-preparation automation. Our analysts viewed this as a strong, generalizable AI automation case study because it shows how domain expertise can be converted into a self-improving agent loop.

items.title: Choosing to Stay Human [ * ]
items.content_text: This article argues that Generative AI should be used intentionally rather than as a default substitute for human thinking, especially in writing and learning. Our analysts emphasized that AI tutors and workplace tools should challenge users rather than simply provide answers, because cognitive effort remains central to learning and competitive advantage.

items.title: From Open Source Software to Open Source Strategy [ * ]
items.content_text: This article frames open source as a strategic tool for commoditizing infrastructure, countering platform control, and shaping AI competition. Our analysts saw it as important context for AI leaders, especially around open weights, open AI ecosystems, and the strategic role of shared infrastructure, even though the piece was less immediately actionable.

items.title: CFOs Funded the AI Revolution. Now They're Joining It [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This article discusses how finance organizations are starting to use AI for workflow redesign, analysis, and faster time to value. Our analysts agreed AI in finance is an important trend, but found the article too high-level and lacking the practical "how" needed for CFOs or AI leaders to act on it.

items.title: Introducing 1-bit and Ternary Bonsai Image 4B: Image Generation for Local Devices [ ~ ]
items.content_text: PrismML introduced compressed 1-bit and ternary versions of Bonsai Image 4B designed to run image generation locally on devices such as iPhones and Macs. Our analysts viewed local AI-driven content creation as important long term, but rated this optional because it is still early and primarily a product announcement.

items.title: Is a Compute Crunch Coming? [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This article examines whether AI inference and training demand could outpace global compute supply. Even though the article sparked a useful debate about token growth, pricing, inference optimization, and chip supply, our analysts rated it optional because its conclusions depended on uncertain assumptions and did not add a crisp action plan.

items.title: Managers Are Struggling to Keep Up with the AI Productivity Boom [ ! ]
items.content_text: This article explains how Generative AI has accelerated individual output so much that managers are becoming the new bottleneck for review, feedback, and validation. Our analysts framed this as an essential organizational shift: AI productivity only scales when management processes change from traditional oversight to faster validation and decision systems.

items.title: D&B's Database of 642 Million Businesses Was Built for Humans, Not AI Agents. So They Rebuilt It. [ ! ]
items.content_text: D&B rebuilt its massive commercial data graph so AI agents can query, resolve, and act on business records rather than relying on human-oriented database structures. Our analysts emphasized this as a major AI infrastructure case study: companies must rebuild data foundations, semantic layers, and agent access patterns before AI automation can scale reliably.

items.title: A Terminal Is All You Need for Web Agents [ * ]
items.content_text: Webwright from Microsoft Research presents a terminal-native approach for web agents, where AI can create reusable scripts, inspect browser sessions, and turn web tasks into repeatable tools. Our analysts highlighted its importance because deterministic code, reusable skills, and better context control could make AI agents more reliable than current browser-clicking approaches.

items.title: How Glance Turns Hours of Video into Mobile-Ready Clips with AI [ * ]
items.content_text: Glance from Google uses AI to convert long-form video into short, vertical, mobile-ready clips by combining speech-to-text, Gemini-based moment selection, speaker detection, reframing, and captions. Our analysts viewed it as a useful AI-driven content creation case study, especially because it shows how probabilistic AI and deterministic editing tools can work together in production.

items.title: Introducing Grok Build [ ~ ]
items.content_text: Grok Build is xAI's early beta coding agent and terminal CLI for software development workflows. Our analysts considered it optional because it is mainly a product announcement and catch-up entry in the AI coding agent market, with limited evidence so far on performance or enterprise readiness.

items.title: Some Ideas for What Comes Next, May 2026 [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This post offers observations on open models, frontier AI systems, product direction, and AI security themes. Our analysts found it to be a useful aggregation of AI news and predictions, but not actionable enough for AI leaders to treat as more than optional reading.

items.title: How I Choose Which Cloudflare Employees to Replace With AI [ ! ]
items.content_text: Cloudflare's CEO explains a framework for using AI automation to reduce roles in middle management, operations, and measurement-heavy functions while continuing to grow elsewhere. Our analysts emphasized that this gives AI leaders a concrete model for evaluating workforce impact, especially around builders, sellers, and coordinating roles.

items.title: The Best Manufacturers Build AI with Workers, Not for Them [ * ]
items.content_text: This HBR article argues that manufacturers should involve frontline workers directly in AI adoption rather than treating AI as top-down replacement automation. Our analysts highlighted the importance of leadership involvement, change management, and worker participation as AI anxiety rises across industries.

items.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills [ * ]
items.content_text: SkillOpt proposes a method for improving agent skills by testing, scoring, and editing skill documents so they perform better across large language models and execution environments. Our analysts emphasized that skills are becoming a critical layer for AI agents, with potential value for transferability, modularity, and avoiding model lock-in.

items.title: I'm the C.E.O. of Goldman Sachs. The A.I. Job Apocalypse Is Overblown. [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This opinion piece argues that fears of an AI job apocalypse are overstated and that labor markets will adapt as they have before. Our analysts viewed the topic as important but found the argument too light and insufficiently actionable for AI leaders.

items.title: Adventhealth Advances Whole-Person Care with OpenAI [ ~ ]
items.content_text: AdventHealth is using ChatGPT in healthcare workflows to reduce administrative burden and return time to clinicians and staff. Our analysts considered the healthcare use case relevant but found the case study too high-level and light on implementation detail.

items.title: How AI Is Forcing McKinsey and Its Peers to Rethink Pricing [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This article examines how generative AI may pressure consulting and professional services firms to move away from hourly billing toward fixed-price or outcome-based models. Our analysts noted that pricing pressure is real, but the article added limited new insight because outcome-based pricing has long been difficult to define and measure.

items.title: An OpenAI Model Has Disproved a Central Conjecture In Discrete Geometry [ ! ]
items.content_text: An OpenAI model helped disprove a long-standing discrete geometry conjecture related to the unit distance problem. Our analysts framed this as a major signal that AI can accelerate discovery by connecting ideas across mathematical and scientific fields to arrive at scientific breakthroughs.

items.title: Qwen3.7: The Agent Frontier [ ! ]
items.content_text: Qwen3.7-Max is Alibaba's new agentic AI model focused on coding, reasoning, tool use, and long-horizon autonomous workflows. Our analysts emphasized its low-cost frontier positioning and relevance for AI leaders evaluating future model mixes for enterprise AI automation.

items.title: Presien Reduces Critical Safety Events on Construction Sites by 70%+ with Claude [ ! ]
items.content_text: Presien uses Claude for real-time construction-site safety monitoring, shifting from manual video review to continuous AI-driven risk detection. Our analysts highlighted this case as a strong example of Generative AI moving beyond knowledge work into physical operations, risk reduction, and continuous feedback loops.

items.title: Meet Stable Audio 3.0, the Model Family Built for Artistic Experimentation with Open-Weight Models [ ~ ]
items.content_text: Stable Audio 3.0 introduces open-weight generative audio models trained on licensed data for music and sound creation. While the licensing and creative AI angle is notable, our analysts concluded that enterprise use cases remain narrow.

items.title: How Ramp Engineers Accelerate Code Review with Codex [ ~ ]
items.content_text: Ramp is using Codex to speed up code review and support internal developer workflows. Our analysts agreed the topic of AI-assisted engineering bottlenecks is important, but the article itself was light on implementation detail and metrics.

items.title: Your AI Change Is Actually a People Change [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This article argues that AI transformation depends as much on people, behavior, and change management as on technology. Our analysts acknowledged the importance of the topic but found the guidance too general and not actionable enough for AI leaders.

items.title: The AI fluency gap between companies [ ! ]
items.content_text: This piece argues that enterprise AI adoption is less about buying tools and more about building institutional fluency, workflow change, and AI-first cultural expectations. The discussion emphasized Zapier as an exemplar: firms with AI-fluent employees can unlock faster prototyping, faster deployment velocity, and broader productivity gains, especially when non-technical teams learn by doing.

items.title: How DoorDash built an AI code reviewer engineers actually listen to [ ! ]
items.content_text: DoorDash's case study shows how an AI code reviewer can improve pull-request quality by tailoring feedback to company-specific engineering practices and institutional knowledge. The key insight is that useful agentic systems must avoid alert fatigue, earn trust, and automate an organization's "cognitive uniqueness" rather than merely applying generic code-review rules.

items.title: Introducing Command A+: Making sovereign agentic capabilities available to all [ * ]
items.content_text: Cohere's Command A+ is positioned as a large multimodal open-weights model aimed at sovereign AI, giving CIOs and CTOs more control over their own AI stack and agentic workloads. Our analysts saw it as important because it supports the long-term theme of "own your own intelligence," while also reflecting a broader race to provide non-Chinese open model alternatives.

items.title: Using Claude Code: The unreasonable effectiveness of HTML [ * ]
items.content_text: Anthropic's article highlights HTML as a richer interface layer for Claude Code outputs, improving on Markdown by supporting more visual, structured, and shareable artifacts. Our analysts stressed that better AI interfaces are central to adoption, especially as larger context windows and agent workflows make human review, collaboration, and non-technical user engagement more important.

items.title: Introducing HRM-Text [ * ]
items.content_text: Sapient Intelligence's HRM-Text is a small 1B-1.5B parameter model using latent reasoning rather than long visible chain-of-thought, pointing toward cheaper and more efficient reasoning architectures. Our analysts treated it as an important wildcard because, while still research-stage and not yet broadly usable, its reported architecture gains could represent an orders-of-magnitude shift if the approach holds up.

items.title: China Wants A.I. to Flourish, but Not at the Expense of Jobs [ ~ ]
items.content_text: The New York Times article examines China's effort to promote AI while limiting job displacement through company-level responsibility and broader labor-policy thinking. The discussion framed it as optional for day-to-day AI leaders, but still valuable as a reminder that responsible AI transformation requires workflow transition planning, not just model deployment or layoffs.

items.title: How Agentic AI Supercharges Startups and Threatens Incumbents [ ! ]
items.content_text: This HBR article explains how agentic AI gives AI-native startups faster iteration, automated go-to-market capabilities, autonomous business functions, capital efficiency, and usage flywheels. Our analysts framed this as a critical strategic warning for incumbents whose legacy data, processes, and business models may slow their response.

items.title: Agents, Human Agency, and the Opportunity for Every Organization [ ! ]
items.content_text: Microsoft outlines how AI agents can expand high-value work and reshape organizations into learning systems. Our analysts emphasized its value for AI leaders managing Copilot adoption, agent identities, permissions, evaluation, and organizational redesign.

items.title: Gemini Omni [ * ]
items.content_text: Gemini Omni is Google DeepMind's new multimodal generative AI model family, starting with video generation and conversational editing from text, image, audio, and video inputs. Our analysts highlighted its importance for AI-driven content creation, especially because consistent characters, physics-aware editing, and reference-based creation could significantly change marketing and media workflows.

items.title: Gemini 3.5 [ * ]
items.content_text: Gemini 3.5 Flash is a new frontier model focused on speed, coding, agentic behavior, and multimodal AI performance. Our analysts rated it important for developers and AI leaders using APIs, while noting that real-world testing is still needed beyond benchmark claims.

items.title: General Agent: A Self-Evolving, Synthetic Agent Environment [ ~ ]
items.content_text: Prime Intellect introduced General Agent, an open synthetic environment for training and evaluating AI agents across thousands of tool-use tasks and domains. Our analysts saw this as an important direction for reinforcement learning, AI automation, and agent orchestration, but still an early product-oriented announcement.

items.title: Index: A Platform for Content Owners [ ~ ]
items.content_text: Index is a platform for content owners to understand how AI agents access and use their work. Our analysts framed it as part of a larger shift toward agent-readable web infrastructure and content compensation, but considered the specific announcement early and product-focused.

items.title: Project Glasswing: What Mythos Showed Us [ ! ]
items.content_text: Project Glasswing details testing of Anthropic's Mythos Preview for AI security and vulnerability research across real infrastructure. Our analysts highlighted security best practices presented in the article such as ability to chain small bugs into more serious exploits, making this essential for leaders thinking about AI-driven cyber defense, adversarial testing, and future security governance.

items.title: How Claude Code Works in Large Codebases: Best Practices and Where to Start [ ! ]
items.content_text: Claude Code's guidance explains how teams can use AI coding tools effectively in large codebases through CLAUDE.md files, hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, LSP integrations, and subagents. Our analysts emphasized that this is essential for developer productivity and AI automation because it gives organizations a practical operating model for scaling agentic coding beyond individual experimentation.

items.title: AI Eats the World [ * ]
items.content_text: This presentation frames Generative AI as a major technology cycle, covering capital investment, deployment, model competition, and enterprise adoption. Our analysts noted that while much of the material is familiar, it is a useful primer for business leaders trying to understand where large language models and AI strategy are heading.

items.title: Starchild-1: The First Real-Time Multimodal World Model [ * ]
items.content_text: Starchild-1 introduces a real-time multimodal world model that generates synchronized audio and video while responding to streaming user input. Our analysts viewed it as a step change for interactive AI-driven content creation, gaming, marketing, robotics, and simulation, though still early for broad enterprise use.

items.title: Introducing Composer 2.5 [ ~ ]
items.content_text: Composer 2.5 is an update to Cursor's AI coding model with improvements in long-running tasks, instruction following, and training methods such as targeted reinforcement learning. Our analysts treated it as incremental rather than a major breakthrough, especially given stronger market attention around competing AI coding tools.

items.title: A New Personal Finance Experience in ChatGPT [ ~ ]
items.content_text: OpenAI is previewing a personal finance experience in ChatGPT that lets U.S. Pro users connect financial accounts, view spending, and ask questions grounded in their financial data. Our analysts found the product direction notable but optional, with privacy, security, and consumer trust concerns limiting its immediate importance for AI leaders.

items.title: How Eightfold Uses Agentic AI To Make Opportunity More Inclusive [ ! ]
items.content_text: Eightfold AI details how it used agentic AI workflows to automate accessibility compliance efforts, specifically addressing WCAG 2.2 standards across its user experience stack. Our analysts highlighted this as a strong "steal it and scale it" enterprise AI case case, showing how scoped AI agents, Jira-integrated workflows, automated testing, and human-in-the-loop review reduced a six-month accessibility remediation process to two months while demonstrating a repeatable AI automation pattern for broader enterprise operations.

items.title: Work with Codex From Anywhere [ * ]
items.content_text: OpenAI introduced expanded Codex remote development capabilities that allow developers to manage coding sessions, SSH environments, shared dev boxes, and automation workflows directly from mobile devices. Our analysts emphasized that this goes beyond simple remote control by enabling persistent multi-environment AI-assisted software engineering workflows, enterprise access controls, programmatic tokens, and continuous twenty-four-by-seven agent management-an important evolution toward AI-managed development operations.

items.title: Introducing PROWL: Learning Through Discovery [ * ]
items.content_text: Odyssey introduced PROWL, a reinforcement learning framework designed to improve world models through prioritized regret-driven optimization that actively searches for novel failures and continuously self-improves. Our analysts viewed this as an important advancement for AI research because the approach could significantly improve robotics, self-driving systems, synthetic environments, and AI-generated simulations by creating dynamic feedback loops that continuously refine model behavior and temporal coherence.

items.title: Gen AI Could Fix Performance Reviews-or Make Them Even Worse [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This article explores how generative AI could improve employee performance reviews by helping managers generate more comprehensive, data-driven evaluations instead of superficial assessments. While our analysts agreed that AI-assisted performance management is an important organizational topic, they felt the article remained too high-level and lacked actionable frameworks or meaningful enterprise AI implementation insights for senior AI leaders.

items.title: Autoscout24 Scales Engineering with AI-Powered Workflows [ ~ ]
items.content_text: AutoScout24 describes how it adopted ChatGPT and Codex to improve engineering workflows and developer productivity across its organization. Our analysts considered the article outdated because it focused primarily on basic AI adoption patterns and AI champions programs rather than delivering deeper lessons on advanced AI automation, measurable engineering transformation, or next-generation enterprise AI practices.

items.title: The End of ERP As We Know It? Five Ways AI Is Disrupting ERP [ ~ ]
items.content_text: This article discusses how AI agents, semantic layers, and headless architectures could eventually transform traditional ERP systems and enterprise software platforms. Although our analysts agreed the broader topic of AI-driven ERP transformation is strategically important, they criticized the article for relying on generalized predictions and platitudes without offering concrete architectural guidance, implementation strategies, or practical enterprise modernization frameworks.

items.title: Beware the Agentic Convergence Trap [ ! ]
items.content_text: This article explains how agentic AI systems can cause competitors to converge on the same strategies when they use similar models, data, objectives, and feedback loops. Our analysts emphasized that AI leaders need to preserve differentiation through proprietary data, human oversight, and carefully designed objective functions rather than blindly automating strategic decisions.

items.title: AutoScientist: Automating the Science of Model Training [ ! ]
items.content_text: AutoScientist is an AI system designed to automate the research loop behind model training, alignment, and self-improvement. Our analysts highlighted its potential importance for companies that want to train or adapt models on proprietary data without relying on scarce frontier-lab expertise, making it relevant to enterprise AI strategy and competitive advantage.
